comment: Machine-readable shape of TODO.json at skill version 1.4.2. Read this when a TODO.json records a different skill_version than the installed skill: there is no backwards compatibility, so the agent holding the file upgrades it or rewrites it.

id.note: stable handle; a sub-task conventionally extends its parent's id

title.note: one line, no trailing full stop

parent.note: id of the task this nests under

note.note: where it got to: a commit, a decision, a reason

blocked_on.note: required non-empty when status is blocked

invariants: every parent names an existing id
no task is its own parent
a blocked task names what it waits on

unversioned.describes: A TODO.json with no skill or skill_version header, an items key instead of tasks, an evidence field instead of note, and no priority or timestamps.
steps: jq --arg now "$now" --arg v 1.4.2 '{skill: "todo", skill_version: $v, comment: (.comment // "Migrated from an unversioned TODO.json."), tasks: [(.items // .tasks)[] | {id, title, status: (if .status == "not-a-defect" then "dropped" else .status end), priority: (.priority // "normal"), parent: (.parent // null), detail: (.detail // null), note: (.note // .evidence // null), blocked_on: (.blocked_on // null), refs: (.refs // []), created_at: (.created_at // $now), updated_at: $now}]}' TODO.json > TODO.json.tmp && mv TODO.json.tmp TODO.json
Then assign real priorities: the migration defaults everything to normal, which is a queue with no order.

if_no_schema_for_a_version: Rewrite the file from the current schema rather than guessing the difference. A register is cheap to rebuild from its own contents and expensive to half-migrate.
